:DISP:GRAD:TIME 1    /*Sets the persistence time to 1 s.*/
:DISP:GRAD:TIME?     /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the waveform brightness, in percent.
remarks: - Values from 1 to 9 are accepted and set to 10, the lowest brightness used.
- A value outside 1 to 100, or one that is not an integer, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the brightness as an integer, for example `60`.
commands.example:
:DISP:WBR 60    /*Sets the waveform brightness to 60%.*/
:DISP:WBR?      /*The query returns 60.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the graticule brightness, in percent.
remarks: - Values from 0 to 9 are accepted and set to 10, the lowest brightness used.
- A value outside 0 to 100, or one that is not an integer, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the brightness as an integer, for example `50`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GBR 50    /*Sets the graticule brightness to 50%.*/
:DISP:GBR?      /*The query returns 50.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the graticule type.
remarks: - FULL: full grid. HALF: light grid. NONE: no grid.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `FULL`, `HALF` or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GRID HALF    /*Selects the light grid.*/
:DISP:GRID?        /*The query returns HALF.*/

commands.desc: Turns the graticule rulers on or off, or queries their state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Turns color grading of the waveform on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - With color grading on, the color of each point shows how often it is hit.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DISP:COL ON    /*Turns color grading on.*/
:DISP:COL?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the brightness of the screen backlight, in percent.
remarks: - A fraction is rounded to the nearest whole percent.
- A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.

commands.desc: Sets or queries what the HDMI output shows: a mirror of the screen, the waveform area, or a layout of its own.
remarks: - The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `MIRROR` and `"Mirror"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `MIRROR`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the text size of the user interface.
remarks: - The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `LARGE` and `"Normal"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `LARGE`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the screen layout.
remarks: - The zoom lane and the per-reference time base belong to the Studio layout.
- The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `STUDIO` and `"Default"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `STUDIO`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the content of the lower pane.
remarks: - The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `RESULTS` and `"Traces"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `RESULTS`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement shown by trend chart 1 of the lower pane.
remarks: - The options are Auto, Off and one per measurement in the measurement list, named by its source and measurement as in the menu (for example `CH1 Vpp`); a pair measurement is named by its name only.
- The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `OFF` and `"Off"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `AUTO` or `CH1_VPP`.
commands.example:
:DISP:TREN1 OFF    /*Hides trend chart 1.*/
:DISP:TREN1?       /*The query returns OFF.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement shown by trend chart 2 of the lower pane.
remarks: - The options are Auto, Off and one per measurement in the measurement list, named by its source and measurement as in the menu (for example `CH1 Vpp`); a pair measurement is named by its name only.
- The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `OFF` and `"Off"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `AUTO` or `CH1_VPP`.
commands.example:
:DISP:TREN2 OFF    /*Hides trend chart 2.*/
:DISP:TREN2?       /*The query returns OFF.*/

commands.desc: Shows a view, or queries which view is shown. Each view is an independent workspace of the one instrument.
remarks: - Channels, time base, trigger, acquisition, the generator output and the math definitions are shared by every view. The measurement list, statistics, panels, cursors, zoom, the references and the bus shown, the analysis setups, which math traces are shown, whether the generator card is shown and the analysis page (`:VIEW`) belong to the view.
- The `:MEASure` commands act on the measurement list of the view shown.
- A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.
commands.example:
:DISP:VIEW:COUN 2    /*Creates a second view.*/
:DISP:VIEW 2         /*Shows view 2.*/
:DISP:VIEW?          /*The query returns 2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of views.
remarks: - Raising the count makes each new view a copy of the view shown.
- A saved setup carries every view.
- A sub-header other than COUNt generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.

commands.desc: Shows or hides the generator chip and card in the view shown, or queries whether they are shown.
remarks: - Only the display changes; the generator output (`:SOURce`) is shared by every view and keeps running.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GEN OFF    /*Hides the generator card.*/
:DISP:GEN?       /*The query returns 0.*/

subsystems.title: :DOCK, :ZOOM and :UI Commands (Screen Layout)
subsystems.intro: These commands work the Studio screen the way a person does: they place, size and float the views (measurement table, eye, second pane, decode table, SIM, histogram, XY, analyser views), run the actions of the plot's right-click menu, and list and press the controls on the screen by name and place. Each runs the same code as the touch it stands for.

commands.desc: Queries where every Studio view is: docked, in a tab group, floating or off, with its rectangle on the screen.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- Rectangles are in screen pixels from the top-left corner; `:UI:SCReen?` gives the screen size.
commands.returns: The query returns one record per view, separated by semicolons: `<name>,<state>,<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>`. `<name>` is WAVE, MEAS, EYE, PANE, TABL, SIM, HIST, XY or VIEW; `<state>` is DOCK, TAB (docked behind another tab of its group, with the group's rectangle), FLOAT or OFF (rectangle 0,0,0,0).

commands.desc: Docks a view against another docked view, or along a whole edge of the area: what dragging the view by its title strip does.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- LEFT, RIGHt, TOP and BOTTom split the target's place 50/50 with `<view>` on that side; CENTer swaps the two views; TABS adds `<view>` to the target's tab group.
- With `<target>` EDGE, `<view>` takes a third of the whole area along that side (two thirds for the waveform), and the rest keeps its arrangement.
- `<view>` must be on the screen and `<target>` docked; otherwise error -221 is generated. A floating view is docked by this command.
commands.example:
:DOCK:MOVE MEAS,WAVE,RIGHT    /*Puts the measurement table to the right of the waveform.*/
:DOCK:MOVE PANE,EDGE,BOTTOM    /*Puts the second pane along the whole bottom edge.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the share of its split a docked view has: what dragging the divider beside it does.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- The least sizes of the views still apply: the divider stops where a view would get smaller than its least size (the waveform 300 x 210 pixels).
- A view in a tab group sizes the whole group.
commands.returns: The query returns the share in scientific notation; `1` when the view fills the area, `0` when it is floating or off.
commands.example:
:DOCK:SIZE MEAS,0.33    /*Gives the measurement table a third of its split.*/
:DOCK:SIZE? MEAS         /*The query returns about 3.300000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Floats a view as a panel at a rectangle, or queries the rectangle of a floating view.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- The panel is kept on the screen and at least its least size (220 x 170 pixels).
- The last docked view cannot float (error -221).
commands.returns: The query returns `<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>`, or `0` when the view is docked.
commands.example: :DOCK:FLOAT PANE,820,90,440,280    /*Floats the second pane in the top-right corner.*/

commands.desc: Shows the measurement table or the SIM view, or queries whether a view is on the screen.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.

- Only MEASurements and SIM are opened by this command; the other views open with their own commands (`:EYE`, `:VIEW`, the decoder and histogram commands), and for them the set only checks that they are on (error -221 when not).
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Closes a view, as the X of its title strip.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- The waveform cannot be closed while it is the plain waveform.

commands.desc: Brings the tab of a view to the front of its tab group.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.

commands.desc: Puts every view in tabs of one group that fills the area, with `<view>` in front (the expand button), or queries whether a view fills the area.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.
- `:DOCK:RESTore` brings back the arrangement from before.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while a view fills the area, otherwise `0`.

commands.desc: Leaves a maximised view and restores the arrangement from before.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.

commands.desc: Returns to the default arrangement: nothing floating, no saved splits.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the whole arrangement as the text the setup keeps.
remarks: - The command needs the Studio layout (`:DISPlay:LAYout STUDio`); in another layout it generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"`.

- The text is the setup's arrangement text with `|` between its parts, because `;` would end the command. Read it, and send it back later to restore an arrangement. An unreadable text gives the default arrangement.
commands.returns: The query returns the arrangement as a quoted string.

commands.desc: Sets or queries whether the traces share one plot or have one lane each (right-click menu: Overlay traces, Stacked traces).
commands.returns: The query returns OVER or STAC.

commands.desc: Fits the whole record into the screen (right-click menu: Fit record).
Opens the zoom window at a time, or moves it there (right-click menu: Zoom here), or queries the centre of the zoom window.
remarks: - Not on analyser views (error -221).
commands.returns: The query returns the centre in seconds in scientific notation.

commands.desc: Zooms on a span of time: the finest zoom step whose window holds the span, centred on it (right-click menu: Zoom box). Queries the zoom window.
remarks: - The window is never slower than the main time base. Not on analyser views (error -221).
commands.returns: The query returns `<t0>,<t1>`, the edges of the zoom window, or `0,0` when zoom is off.

commands.desc: Returns the zoom window to its default size and place (right-click menu: Reset zoom).
Closes the zoom window (right-click menu: Close zoom).
Queries the size of the screen in pixels.
commands.returns: The query returns `<w>,<h>`.

commands.desc: Queries every control on the screen now, with its label and rectangle, so that a program can find a button and press it.
remarks: - TOP: top bar buttons. BOTTOM: channel, reference and math chips, time and trigger. VIEW: each view, labelled `Name (WAVE)`. CLOSE, EXPAND, TAB: the buttons and tabs of the title strips. RESIZE: the corner of a floating panel. DIVIDER: the touch area of a divider. BADGE: measurement badges. CURSOR: cursor tags. MENU: the rows of the menu that is open.
- Press an element with `:UI:TAP` at the centre of its rectangle.
commands.returns: The query returns one record per element, separated by semicolons: `<kind>,"<label>",<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>`.

commands.desc: Taps the screen at a point, as a finger.
Drags a finger from one point to another in steps: moves a divider, a view by its strip, a floating panel by its corner, a cursor.
commands.example: :UI:DRAG 850,300,700,300    /*Drags a vertical divider 150 pixels to the left.*/

commands.desc: Opens the menu a right click or a held finger opens at a point: the menu of the plot, of a channel chip or of a view.
remarks: - `:UI:MENU?` then lists its rows, and `:UI:MENU:SELect` presses one.

commands.desc: Queries the menu or popup that is open, with its rows.
commands.returns: The query returns the title, then each row, as quoted strings separated by commas. A side menu lists its items as `"<label> = <value>"`. `""` when no menu is open.

commands.desc: Presses the row of the open menu with a label.
params: A row label; case does not matter, a unique beginning is enough
remarks: - With no menu open, error -221 is generated; an unknown or ambiguous label generates -224.

commands.desc: Closes whatever menu or popup is open.

subsystems.title: :MEASure Commands
subsystems.intro: The :MEASure commands add measurement items to the readout, query measurement results and statistics, and set the measurement thresholds, sources and range. Standard items are listed in Appendix A and pair items in Appendix B.

commands.desc: Adds the specified measurement item to the measurement readout, or queries the measurement result of the specified item. Standard items take one source; pair items (delay, phase, skew, setup and hold) take source A and source B. The query computes the value directly and does not require the item to be on the readout.
params: Standard items: refer to Appendix A. Pair items: refer to Appendix B.
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; pair items only
remarks: - Item names are accepted in long or short form, case-insensitively (for example `FREQuency` or `FREQ`).
- Set form: adding an item that is already on the readout with the same sources keeps the existing row and its statistics; no second row is created.

- Set form: when the readout already holds the maximum number of rows (1024 in total for standard, pair and catalogue rows), a standard item raises `-223,"Measurement selection is full"`; a pair item raises `-224,"Measurement selection is full"`.
- Set form: a pair item whose source A and source B are the same raises `-224,"Source A and B are the same source"`. More sources than the item takes raise `-224,"Too many measurement sources"`.

- Query form: a standard item without a source uses the :MEASure:SOURce A selection. A pair item query requires both <srcA> and <srcB>; if <srcB> is missing, `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` is raised and `9.9E37` is returned.

- Query form: `SETHold` (alias `SHOLD`, query only) accepts either no sources (the Measure A and B selections are used) or exactly two sources (clock, data); any other count raises `-224` and returns `9.9E37`.

- For SETUP/HOLD/SETHOLD, FSETUP/FHOLD and DSETUP/DHOLD/DSETHOLD, source A is the clock (strobe) and source B is the data. SETUP/HOLD latch on rising clock edges, FSETUP/FHOLD on falling edges and the `D` items on both strobe edges, as a DDR DQS strobe does. A clock edge counts only when the data changed within that edge's own cycle; data that holds steady between strobe bursts adds no setup or hold result.
- SETHOLD and DSETHOLD return the number of latching edges that violate the :MEASure:TSETup or :MEASure:THOLd limit.
- An unknown item, or a source token that is not `CHAN<n>`/`R<n>`/`REF<n>`, raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- The measured span is controlled by :MEASure:GATing.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the measurement value in scientific notation in base units (V, s, Hz, %, degrees, V*s, V/s, or a count), for example `1.966000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:ITEM VPP,CHAN1    /*Adds Vpp of CH1 to the measurement readout.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 3.300000E+00.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? RRDELAY,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*The query returns 2.500000E-09.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DSETUP,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*CH1 = DQS strobe, CH2 = DQ data, both strobe edges. The query returns 1.966000E-10.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DHOLD,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*The query returns 2.140000E-10.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DSETHOLD,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Number of strobe edges violating TSETup/THOLd. The query returns 0.000000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the default measurement source. The optional second source sets the default source B used by pair items.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source A is the same setting as :MEASure:SETup:PSA (:MEASure:SETup:DSA); source B is the same setting as :MEASure:SETup:PSB (:MEASure:SETup:DSB).
- An empty argument, more than two sources, or an invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and nothing is changed.
commands.returns: The query returns source A only, as `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SOUR CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Sets source A to CH1 and source B to CH2.*/
:MEAS:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Removes all measurement items from the readout.
remarks: - Standard, pair and catalogue rows are all removed, together with their per-row settings.
- DVM and counter rows on the readout are controlled by :DVM:ENABle and :COUNter:ENABle and are not affected.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement range. `SCReen` measures only the part of the record visible in the current view; `NONE` measures the full record.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `SCREEN` or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:GAT NONE    /*Measures over the full record.*/
:MEAS:GAT?    /*The query returns NONE.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the low/high edge threshold pair, in percent of the waveform amplitude, used by edge measurements such as rise and fall time.
remarks: - Spaces in the argument are ignored. `10/90`, `1090` and `10` set 10 % and 90 %; `20/80`, `2080` and `20` set 20 % and 80 %.

- This command sets the same thresholds as :MEASure:SETup:MIN and :MEASure:SETup:MAX. The query returns `10/90` when the low threshold is below 15 % and the high threshold above 85 %; any other combination is reported as `20/80`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new thresholds.
commands.returns: The query returns `10/90` or `20/80`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:REFS 20/80    /*Sets the thresholds to 20 % and 80 %.*/
:MEAS:REFS?    /*The query returns 20/80.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the upper threshold of the measurement, in percent of the waveform amplitude.
params: 0 to 100; must be greater than the lower threshold
remarks: - A value outside 0 to 100 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. A value not greater than the current lower threshold raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value" below the lower threshold`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new threshold.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold as an integer percent, rounded, for example `90`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:MAX 80    /*Sets the upper threshold to 80 %.*/
:MEAS:SET:MAX?    /*The query returns 80.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the lower threshold of the measurement, in percent of the waveform amplitude.
params: 0 to 100; must be less than the upper threshold
remarks: - A value outside 0 to 100 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. A value not less than the current upper threshold raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value" above the upper threshold`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new threshold.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold as an integer percent, rounded, for example `10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:MIN 20    /*Sets the lower threshold to 20 %.*/
:MEAS:SET:MIN?    /*The query returns 20.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source A of the phase and delay measurements.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source A is the same setting as the source set by :MEASure:SOURce; changing one changes the other.
- An invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:PSA CHAN1    /*Sets source A to CH1.*/
:MEAS:SET:PSA?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source B of the phase and delay measurements.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source B is used by pair items added or queried without an explicit second source (for example by :MEASure:ITEM and by the SETHold query without sources).
- An invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:PSB CHAN2    /*Sets source B to CH2.*/
:MEAS:SET:PSB?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the setup-time limit, in seconds, used by the SETHOLD and DSETHOLD violation counts.
remarks: - A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the limit in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:TSET 2E-10    /*Sets the setup limit to 200 ps.*/
:MEAS:TSET?    /*The query returns 2.000000E-10.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the hold-time limit, in seconds, used by the SETHOLD and DSETHOLD violation counts.
remarks: - A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the limit in scientific notation, for example `1.500000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:THOL 1.5E-10    /*Sets the hold limit to 150 ps.*/
:MEAS:THOL?    /*The query returns 1.500000E-10.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the burst idle interval, in seconds, used to separate bursts for the burst width (BWIDth) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new interval.
- A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the interval in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-06`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:BURS:IDLE 1E-6    /*Sets the idle interval to 1 us.*/
:MEAS:BURS:IDLE?    /*The query returns 1.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries which side of the threshold levels is counted by the time-outside (TOUTside) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `ABOV`, `BEL` or `BOTH`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:OUTS ABOV    /*Counts time above the upper level only.*/
:MEAS:OUTS?    /*The query returns ABOV.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of edge intervals spanned by the duration-of-N-periods (NPERiods) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- A value outside 1 to 32 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `4`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:NPER 4    /*Measures the duration of 4 periods.*/
:MEAS:NPER?    /*The query returns 4.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the edges used by the duration-of-N-periods (NPERiods) measurement. `CLOCk` uses rising mid-level crossings only; `DATA` uses mid-level crossings in either direction.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CLOC` or `DATA`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:EDG DATA    /*Uses both edge directions.*/
:MEAS:EDG?    /*The query returns DATA.*/

commands.desc: Turns on or off the measurement indicators (labels drawn on the trace), or queries their status.
remarks: - :CURSor:MEASure:INDicator controls the same setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:IND ON    /*Turns on the measurement indicators.*/
:MEAS:IND?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Queries every row of the measurement readout and its current value in one reply.
remarks: - Rows are listed in this order: standard rows, pair rows, catalogue rows, then the DVM row (only while :DVM:ENABle is ON) and the counter row (only while :COUNter:ENABle is ON).
- The item token is the canonical upper-case long form (for example `FREQUENCY`, `RRDELAY`); refer to Appendix A and Appendix B.
- Catalogue rows (analysis items selected on the measurement catalogue, Appendix D) cannot be queried individually with :MEASure:ITEM?; read them here.
- When the readout is empty, the reply is an empty line.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns:
The query returns the rows separated by `;`. Row formats:
Standard: `<ITEM>,<src>,<value>`
Pair: `<ITEM>,<srcA>,<srcB>,<value>`
Catalogue: `CAT<id>,<srcA>,<srcB>,<srcC>,<srcD>,<value>` (unused source roles are still listed)
DVM: `DVM,<DC|ACRMS|ACDC>,CHAN<n>,<value>`
Counter: `COUNTER,<FREQUENCY|PERIOD|TOTALIZE>,CHAN<n>,<value>`
Sources are `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`; values are in scientific notation.

commands.desc: Queries every measurement shown on the screen: the measurement readout rows and, while the Eye page is displayed, every Eye figure.
remarks: - The Eye figures are appended only while :VIEW? returns `EYE`; refer to Appendix C for the figure names.
- When nothing is shown, the reply is an empty line.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the :MEASure:STRip? rows followed by one `<FIGURE>,<value>` row per Eye figure (figure name in upper-case long form, for example `HEIGHT`), all separated by `;`. Values are in scientific notation.
commands.example: :MEAS:READ?    /*With the Eye page displayed, the query returns VPP,CHAN1,3.300000E+00;ONE,1.200000E+00;ZERO,1.000000E-01;...;NPJ,9.9E37.*/

commands.desc: Turns on or off the statistics display of the measurement readout, or queries its status.
remarks: - Hiding the statistics keeps the accumulated observations; they are shown again when the display is turned back on.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:DISP ON    /*Shows the measurement statistics.*/
:MEAS:STAT:DISP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Clears the statistics history of all measurement rows.
remarks: - The rows themselves stay on the readout. No new acquisition is started.

commands.desc: Adds the specified measurement item to the readout and turns on the statistics display, or queries one statistic of the specified item.
params: Standard items: refer to Appendix A. Pair items: refer to Appendix B.
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; pair items only
remarks: - Set form: behaves as :MEASure:ITEM (same errors); the statistics display is turned on only if no error was raised.
- Query form: `CNT` and `COUNt` return the number of observations. A row that is not on the readout has a count of 0 and `9.9E37` for the other statistics.
- `DEViation` (standard deviation) needs more than one observation; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- The current value uses the row's own settings on the readout where applicable.
- An invalid <type>, item or source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and returns `9.9E37`. An unknown node below :MEASure:STATistic raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the statistic in scientific notation; the count is also returned in scientific notation, for example `1.200000E+01`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM VPP,CHAN1    /*Adds Vpp of CH1 and shows statistics.*/
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM? MAX,VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 3.312000E+00.*/
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM? CNT,VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 1.200000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Copies the measurements of the current Source A to another source, like Copy to in the Measure menu.
remarks: - The target must be a source the menu offers (an input of the model, or a loaded reference) and not Source A itself; otherwise the command generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- Source A is set with `:MEASure:SOURce`.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SOUR CHAN1
:MEAS:COPY CHAN2    /*Adds the CH1 measurements for CH2 as well.*/

commands.desc: Removes one measurement from the list, by its position or by item and source.
params: 1 to the number of measurements, in :MEASure:STRip? order
remarks: - A pair measurement (delay or phase) takes two sources.
- When no measurement matches, the command generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:ITEM:REM 1            /*Removes the first measurement.*/
:MEAS:ITEM:REM VPP,CHAN2    /*Removes Vpp of CH2.*/

commands.desc: Adds a measurement of the six-tab measurement catalogue by its number, or queries its value.
params: A number of the measurement catalogue
The current sources A, B, C and D
remarks: - The sources that are not given are the current Source A and Source B (`:MEASure:SETup:PSA`, `:MEASure:SETup:PSB`) and Source C and D (`:MEASure:CATalog:SOURceC`, `:MEASure:CATalog:SOURceD`). The current sources are not changed.
- A row that is already in the list is not added twice.
- The rows appear in `:MEASure:STRip?` and `:MEASure:READout?` as `CAT<id>,A,B,C,D,value`.
- An unknown number or source generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when no value exists.
commands.example:
:MEAS:CAT:ITEM 1,CHAN1     /*Adds catalogue row 1 on CH1.*/
:MEAS:CAT:ITEM? 1,CHAN1    /*The query returns its value, for example 2.500000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries Source C of the measurement catalogue, used by catalogue rows that need more than two sources.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) is accepted only while that reference slot holds a waveform.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:CAT:SOURC CHAN2    /*Sets Source C to CH2.*/
:MEAS:CAT:SOURC?         /*The query returns CH2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries Source D of the measurement catalogue, used by catalogue rows that need more than two sources.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) is accepted only while that reference slot holds a waveform.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:CAT:SOURD CHAN2    /*Sets Source D to CH2.*/
:MEAS:CAT:SOURD?         /*The query returns CH2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries whether the reference levels of the measurements are given in percent of the waveform or in volts.
remarks: - Each type keeps its own set of levels.
- The long or the short form of the keyword is accepted.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `PERC` or `VOLT`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:LEV:TYPE VOLT    /*Gives the levels in volts.*/
:MEAS:LEV:TYPE?        /*The query returns VOLT.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the preset of the low and high reference levels.
remarks: - 10/90 and 20/80 set the low and high levels in percent; CUSTom keeps the levels set with `:MEASure:LEVel:LOW` and `:MEASure:LEVel:HIGH`. `1090` and `2080` are also accepted, and spaces are ignored.
- Setting a low or high level selects CUSTom.
- This is the same setting as `:MEASure:REFS`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `10/90`, `20/80` or `CUSTOM`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:LEV:PRES 20/80    /*Sets the levels to 20 % and 80 %.*/
:MEAS:LEV:PRES?         /*The query returns 20/80.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the low reference level of the measurements.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- Setting this level selects the CUSTom preset (`:MEASure:LEVel:PRESet`).
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `15`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the middle reference level of the measurements.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `45`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the high reference level of the measurements.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- Setting this level selects the CUSTom preset (`:MEASure:LEVel:PRESet`).
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `85`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the hysteresis of the edge detection of the measurements.
remarks: - With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.
- A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the hysteresis as a plain number, for example `5`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries how the base and top of the waveform are found.
remarks: - MINMax takes the base and top from the minimum and maximum of the waveform, MEAN and MODE from the mean or the most frequent values of the samples; AUTO chooses the method.
- The long or the short form of the keyword is accepted.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `AUTO`, `MINM`, `MEAN` or `MODE`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:LEV:BASE MINM    /*Uses the minimum and maximum.*/
:MEAS:LEV:BASE?        /*The query returns MINM.*/

commands.desc: Gives the falling edges their own reference levels, or queries whether they have them.
remarks: - When on, falling edges use the levels set with `:MEASure:LEVel:FALL:LOW`, `:MID` and `:HIGH`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:LEV:FALL:SEP ON    /*Uses separate levels for falling edges.*/
:MEAS:LEV:FALL:SEP?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the low reference level of falling edges.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The level is used when `:MEASure:LEVel:FALL:SEParate` is ON.
- The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `20`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the middle reference level of falling edges.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The level is used when `:MEASure:LEVel:FALL:SEParate` is ON.
- The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `50`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the high reference level of falling edges.
params: Percent: 1 to 99; volts: any finite value
remarks: - The level is used when `:MEASure:LEVel:FALL:SEParate` is ON.
- The levels are shared by all measurements. With `:MEASure:LEVel:TYPE PERCent` the value is in percent of the base-to-top amplitude; with VOLTs it is in volts.

- The low, middle and high levels must stay in that order (low < mid < high); in percent they must also be within 1 to 99. A value that breaks the order, or is not a number, is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the level as a plain number, for example `80`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries which acquisitions the measurement statistics cover.
remarks: - CURRent: the acquisitions of the current run. ACCumulated: every acquisition since the statistics were last reset.
- A change resets the statistics.
- The long or the short form of the keyword is accepted.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CURR` or `ACC`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:POP CURR    /*Statistics of the current run.*/
:MEAS:STAT:POP?        /*The query returns CURR.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the columns shown in the statistics of the measurement list.
remarks: - The columns not given are hidden; NONE hides all three.
- The long or the short form of each keyword is accepted. An unknown column is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the shown columns separated by commas, in the order `SDEV`, `MIN`, `MAX`, or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:SHOW MIN,MAX    /*Shows the minimum and the maximum.*/
:MEAS:STAT:SHOW?           /*The query returns MIN,MAX.*/

subsystems.title: :EYE Commands
subsystems.intro: The :EYE command queries the figures of the Eye diagram analysis. The Eye figures are listed in Appendix C.

commands.desc: Queries one figure of the current Eye diagram result, such as eye height, eye width, unit interval or total jitter.
remarks: - Figure names are accepted in long or short form, case-insensitively. Any text after a comma is ignored.
- The query reads the result of the Eye analysis as currently configured; it does not run the one-click Auto Eye.

- A full-record Eye of a long reference is calculated in the background. Until it finishes, the previous result is returned; check that `EDGES` and `UI` belong to the new source before reading the other figures.
- With an Eye clock source such as a DDR DQS strobe, the data is folded on each strobe edge, so bursts that start at unrelated phases line up as the receiver latches them.
- An unknown figure raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the figure in scientific notation, for example `3.125000E-10`.
commands.example:
:VIEW EYE    /*Displays the Eye page.*/
:EYE:ITEM? WIDTH    /*The query returns 2.410000E-10.*/

commands.desc: Sets up the Eye and jitter analysis from the signal, like Auto Eye/Jitter in the Eye menu.
remarks: - The analysis uses the source set with `:EYE:SOURce`.
- This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Clears the accumulated eye and starts it again.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the data signal of the Eye analysis.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) selects a reference slot that holds a waveform.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the clock or strobe signal whose edges fold the eye (for example DQS or a forwarded clock). OFF folds on the clock recovered from the data.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) selects a reference slot that holds a waveform.
- OFF (or NONE) leaves the input unused.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`, or `OFF`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the second line of a differential pair or another rail used for the common-mode figures.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) selects a reference slot that holds a waveform.
- OFF (or NONE) leaves the input unused.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`, or `OFF`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the bit rate of the Eye analysis, in bit/s.
remarks: - Setting a rate stops taking the rate from the whole record.
- A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the rate in scientific notation, for example `1.600000E+09`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the bit error ratio at which total jitter, eye width and eye height are given. J2 and J9 do not use it.
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-15`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the lower offset frequency of the phase-noise integration, in hertz.
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+04`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the upper offset frequency of the phase-noise integration, in hertz.
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+07`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries a frequency, in hertz, removed from the time interval error as a sine (for example a known spread-spectrum or supply tone).
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `3.300000E+04`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the closed-loop bandwidth of the PLL that recovers the clock, in hertz.
params: 0 Hz to 1E+08 Hz; 0 = the bit rate / 1667
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+06`.

commands.desc: Turns the non-periodic jitter figure on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Turns the 30 kHz high-pass filter of the common-mode figures on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries where the eye is drawn: over the full plot area, beside the trace or under it.
remarks: - The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `SIDE` and `"SIDE"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `SIDE`.

subsystems.title: Analysis Page Commands
subsystems.intro: These commands query results of the analysis pages (:POWer, :SPECtrum, :MAGnetic, :INVerter, :DPT, :BANDwidth), control the Bode sweep (:BODE) and select the displayed page (:VIEW). They are OOS extensions. The analysis items are listed in Appendix D.

commands.desc: Queries one power analysis result, such as real power, power factor, switching loss or ripple.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Item names are matched case-insensitively and must be given in full (no short forms).
- The number of sources depends on the item (refer to Appendix D): most items take none or two (voltage, current); ripple and inrush items take none or one; rail items take up to three.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `1.250000E+01`.
commands.example: :POW:ITEM? REAL,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Real power with V on CH1 and I on CH2. The query returns 1.250000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current harmonics of the specified source, up to the 40th order.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
The current source of the Power page
remarks: - When the source is omitted, the current source configured on the Power page is used.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no harmonics can be calculated.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
commands.returns: The query returns `<order>,<amplitude>` pairs separated by `;`; the order is an integer and the rms amplitude (A) is in scientific notation.

commands.desc: Queries one spectrum analysis result, such as THD, SNR, SFDR, ENOB or ACPR.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Item names are matched case-insensitively and must be given in full.
- When the distortion analysis cannot run on the source data, `9.9E37` is returned without an error, even for an unknown item.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `-6.523000E+01`.

commands.desc: Queries one magnetic analysis result: inductance, peak flux density, peak field strength, relative permeability or core loss.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Either no sources or exactly two (voltage, current) are accepted.
- Results that depend on the core geometry (turns, effective area, effective length) return `9.9E37` until that geometry is configured on the Magnetic page.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `4.700000E-05`.

commands.desc: Queries one inverter/motor analysis result, such as d/q components, electrical frequency, speed, torque, power or efficiency.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Accepted source counts: none; one (the analog angle input, only when the angle mode is Analog); three (phases A, B, C); or four (A, B, C, angle).
- Sources are refused when the angle mode is Quadrature or Hall.
- `DIR` returns a word instead of a number.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `1.500000E+03`. For `DIR` the query returns `FORWARD`, `REVERSE` or `STOPPED`.
commands.example:
:INV:ITEM? SPEED    /*The query returns 1.500000E+03.*/
:INV:ITEM? DIR    /*The query returns FORWARD.*/

commands.desc: Queries one double-pulse test result, such as turn-on/turn-off energy, switching times, dv/dt, di/dt or reverse recovery.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; gate source
remarks: - Either no sources, two (voltage, current) or three (voltage, current, gate) are accepted.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `2.350000E-04`.

commands.desc: Queries one step-response bandwidth estimate: rise time, bandwidth derived from the rise time, or overshoot.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - The source must contain at least 1000 samples; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `3.500000E+08`.

commands.desc: Starts or stops the Bode (frequency response) sweep.
remarks: - A missing argument is treated as ON.
- The sweep state changes only when it differs from the requested state.
- The sweep drives the signal generator configured with :BODE:GENerator and controls the acquisition.
- An invalid argument generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while the sweep runs, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:BODE:RUN ON    /*Starts the Bode sweep.*/
:BODE:RUN?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Queries the points of the Bode sweep.
remarks: - In `LOOP` and `PSRR` modes the gain is in dB; in `IMPedance` mode it is the linear Vout/Vin ratio.
- The frequency is printed with 6 significant digits and no trailing zeros (for example `1000`, `1258.93`). The gain has 3 decimals and the phase (degrees, -180 to 180) 2 decimals.
- A phase that could not be determined is printed as `NaN`.
- When the sweep has no points, the reply is an empty line.
commands.returns: The query returns the points separated by `;`, each as `<freq>,<gain>,<phase>` in fixed-point notation.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the Bode measurement mode: control-loop response, power-supply rejection ratio or impedance.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `LOOP`, `PSRR` or `IMP`.
commands.example:
:BODE:MODE PSRR    /*Selects PSRR mode.*/
:BODE:MODE?    /*The query returns PSRR.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the signal generator driven by the Bode sweep: its network address (`ip:port`), or `usb` for the first USBTMC generator on the USB-A port.
params: `ip:port` or `usb`, one word; enclosing quotes are removed
remarks: - `usb` is not case-sensitive. The network address is kept while `usb` is selected.
- An address containing whitespace raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the address without quotes, for example `192.168.1.100:5555`, or `usb`.
commands.example:
:BODE:GEN "192.168.1.50:5555"    /*Sets the generator address.*/
:BODE:GEN?                       /*The query returns 192.168.1.50:5555.*/
:BODE:GEN usb                    /*Uses the generator on the USB-A port.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the page shown in the main window: the oscilloscope or one of the analysis pages.
remarks: - BWTest is the bandwidth test page (see also `:BANDwidth:STATe`).
- :MEASure:READout? includes the Eye figures only while the view is `EYE`.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.

subsystems.title: :SPECtrum Commands

commands.desc: Sets the centre frequency to the highest peak of the spectrum, like Centre on peak.

commands.desc: Makes a limit line from the current trace plus the margin set with `:SPECtrum:LIMit:MARGin`, like Limit from trace.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries how far above the trace the limit line is placed by `:SPECtrum:LIMit:SET`, in dB.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the signal of the spectrum analysis.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the window function of the spectrum.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the trace mode of the spectrum.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the channel width of the adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR), in hertz.

subsystems.title: :MAGnetic Commands

subsystems.title: :INVerter Commands

commands.desc: Sets or queries the page of the inverter and motor analysis.

commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `MECHANICAL`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the signal of phase A.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) selects a reference slot that holds a waveform.

commands.returns: The query returns `CH<n>` or `R<n>`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the signal of phase B.
remarks: - `CHANnel<n>` (or `CHAN<n>`) selects an input of the model; `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`) selects a reference slot that holds a waveform.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the signal of phase C.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the scale of the analog angle sensor signal.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the angle per volt of the analog angle sensor, in degrees per volt.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the offset added to the rotor angle, in degrees.

commands.desc: Sets or queries whether the phase signals are voltages or currents.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the torque sensor signal of the Mechanical page.

commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the channel of the bandwidth test.
remarks: - Only channels of the model are accepted.
- A change clears the result.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the expected bandwidth that sets up the test, in hertz.
remarks: - The value is set to the nearest of the offered values (0 = automatic, then 1 MHz to 1 GHz).
- A change clears the result.
- A negative value or a value that is not a number generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+08`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of frequency bins of the bandwidth test.
remarks: - The value is set to the nearest of the listed values.
- A change clears the result.
- A value below 1 or a value that is not a number generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.

subsystems.title: :CURSor Commands
subsystems.intro: The :CURSor commands set the cursor mode, sources and positions and query the cursor values. In the headers below, `<type>` stands for `MANual`, `TRACk` or `XY`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the cursor mode.
remarks: - `MANual` keeps the current manual cursor type: amplitude cursors stay amplitude cursors, otherwise time cursors are used.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. :CURSor without a node raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `OFF`, `MAN`, `TRAC` or `XY`.
commands.example:
:CURS:MODE MAN    /*Selects manual cursors.*/
:CURS:MODE?    /*The query returns MAN.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the type of the manual cursors: time (X) or amplitude (Y).
remarks: - Setting the type also selects manual mode, except in XY mode, where the command is accepted but has no effect.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `AMPL` while amplitude cursors are active, otherwise `TIME`.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:TYPE AMPL    /*Selects amplitude cursors.*/
:CURS:MAN:TYPE?    /*The query returns AMPL.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of cursor A (manual mode: the source of both cursors).
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; the channel must exist on the model and the reference must be loaded
remarks: - Selecting a cursor source does not change the acquisition.
- A token that is not a valid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; a channel not present on the model or an empty reference raises `-224,"Cursor source is unavailable or unsupported"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the cursor A source to CH1.*/
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of track cursor B, independently of cursor A.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Until a B source is set, cursor B follows the cursor A source.

- Manual cursors share one source: :CURSor:MANual:SOURce2 is accepted only when it names the current cursor A source (no change), otherwise it raises `-224,"Cursor source is unavailable or unsupported"`; its query returns the cursor A source.
- A token that is not a valid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR2 CHAN2    /*Sets the track cursor B source to CH2.*/
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR2?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the time (s) position of cursor A.
params: Finite time (s), limited to the visible span
remarks: - The time is converted to a screen position and limited to the visible time span.
- Setting a time while the cursors are OFF selects manual time cursors; while amplitude cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the voltage positions are kept.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `-2.000000E-06`; `9.9E37` when no time cursor is placed.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the time (s) position of cursor B.
params: Finite time (s), limited to the visible span
remarks: - The time is converted to a screen position and limited to the visible time span.
- Setting a time while the cursors are OFF selects manual time cursors; while amplitude cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the voltage positions are kept.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `3.000000E-06`; `9.9E37` when no time cursor is placed.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the voltage (V) position of cursor A.
params: Finite voltage (V), limited to the displayed range
remarks: - The voltage is limited to the displayed range of the cursor source, including display zoom.
- Setting a voltage while the cursors are OFF selects manual amplitude cursors; while time or track cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the time positions are kept.
- The query returns `9.9E37` in OFF, time and track modes.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `1.200000E+00`; `9.9E37` when no voltage cursor is placed.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the voltage (V) position of cursor B.
params: Finite voltage (V), limited to the displayed range
remarks: - The voltage is limited to the displayed range of the cursor source, including display zoom.
- Setting a voltage while the cursors are OFF selects manual amplitude cursors; while time or track cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the time positions are kept.
- The query returns `9.9E37` in OFF, time and track modes.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `-4.000000E-01`; `9.9E37` when no voltage cursor is placed.

commands.desc: Queries the time value of cursor A.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the cursors are OFF or amplitude cursors are active.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the time value of cursor B.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the cursors are OFF or amplitude cursors are active.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the Y value of cursor A.
remarks: - In XY and amplitude modes, the cursor's voltage position is returned. In time and track modes, the waveform value of the cursor source at the cursor A time is returned. When the cursors are OFF, `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the Y value of cursor B.
remarks: - As :CURSor:<type>:AYValue? for cursor B. In track mode the waveform value is taken from the cursor B source (:CURSor:TRACk:SOURce2).
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the time difference between cursor B and cursor A (tB - tA).
remarks: - Available in time, track and XY modes; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the reciprocal of the absolute time difference between the cursors, 1/|tB - tA|.
remarks: - Available in time, track and XY modes when the difference is not zero; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

commands.desc: Queries the Y difference between cursor B and cursor A (yB - yA).
remarks: - In track mode, `9.9E37` is returned when the A and B sources have different units.
- `9.9E37` is returned when either Y value is unavailable.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.

subsystems.title: :DVM Commands
subsystems.intro: The :DVM commands control the digital voltmeter and query its reading.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the digital voltmeter, or queries its status.
remarks: - While the DVM is on, its reading is also listed by :MEASure:STRip?.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DVM:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the DVM.*/
:DVM:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the digital voltmeter.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:DVM:SOUR CHAN2    /*Sets the DVM source to CH2.*/
:DVM:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the mode of the digital voltmeter: `DC` (average), `ACRMs` (AC rms) or `ACDCrms` (rms including DC).
remarks: - `ACRMS` and `ACDC` are also accepted.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `DC`, `ACRMS` or `ACDC`.
commands.example:
:DVM:MODE ACRM    /*Selects AC rms.*/
:DVM:MODE?    /*The query returns ACRMS.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current reading of the digital voltmeter, in volts.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the source channel is off or no reading is available.
commands.returns: The query returns the voltage in scientific notation, for example `1.650000E+00`.

subsystems.title: :COUNter Commands
subsystems.intro: The :COUNter commands control the frequency counter and query its reading.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the frequency counter, or queries its status.
remarks: - While the counter is on, its reading is also listed by :MEASure:STRip?.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:COUN:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the counter.*/
:COUN:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the frequency counter.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:COUN:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the counter source to CH1.*/
:COUN:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement mode of the frequency counter: frequency, period or totalize (edge count).
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `FREQ`, `PER` or `TOT`.
commands.example:
:COUN:MODE PER    /*Selects period mode.*/
:COUN:MODE?    /*The query returns PER.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of digits shown by the frequency counter.
remarks: - A value outside 3 to 7 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `6`.

commands.desc: Queries the current reading of the frequency counter.
remarks: - The unit depends on :COUNter:MODE: Hz (frequency), s (period) or a number of edges (totalize).
- `9.9E37` is returned when the counter is off, the source channel is off, or no reading is available.
commands.returns: The query returns the reading in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+06`.

commands.desc: Clears the totalized count and the counter statistics.

subsystems.title: :HISTogram Commands
subsystems.intro: The :HISTogram commands control the waveform histogram and query its statistics.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the histogram, or queries its status.
remarks: - Turning the histogram on while it is off selects a vertical histogram.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:HIST:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the histogram.*/
:HIST:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the histogram type: horizontal (time distribution) or vertical (voltage distribution).
remarks: - Setting a type also turns the histogram on.
- The query returns `VERT` also while the histogram is off.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `HOR` or `VERT`.
commands.example:
:HIST:TYPE HOR    /*Selects a horizontal histogram.*/
:HIST:TYPE?    /*The query returns HOR.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the histogram.
remarks: - The histogram uses the measurement source A. Setting the histogram source turns that channel on and makes it the :MEASure:SOURce A selection.
- The query returns the measurement source when that channel is on, otherwise the first channel that is on, or `CHAN1` when no channel is on.
- Only analog channels are accepted. An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:HIST:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the histogram source to CH1.*/
:HIST:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Queries the statistics of the histogram.
remarks: - The statistics describe the histogram as displayed, for the current view and zoom, not every sample of the full record.
- Values are in volts for a vertical histogram and in seconds for a horizontal histogram.
- Undefined figures are returned as `9.9E37`. While the histogram is off, the reply is `Sum:0,Peaks:0` followed by `9.9E37` for every other figure.
commands.returns: The query returns `Sum:<n>,Peaks:<n>,Max:<v>,Min:<v>,Pk_Pk:<v>,Mean:<v>,Median:<v>,Mode:<v>,Bin width:<v>,Sigma:<v>`, where `<n>` is an integer and `<v>` is in scientific notation.

subsystems.title: :MASK Commands
subsystems.intro: The :MASK commands control the pass/fail mask test and query its results.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the pass/fail mask test, or queries its status.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MASK:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the mask test.*/
:MASK:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the mask test.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references and math are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:MASK:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the mask source to CH1.*/
:MASK:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal tolerance of the mask, in divisions.
remarks: - If a mask has already been created, it is rebuilt with the new tolerance.
- A value out of range raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the tolerance in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:MASK:X 0.24    /*Sets the horizontal tolerance to 0.24 div.*/
:MASK:X?    /*The query returns 2.400000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical tolerance of the mask, in divisions.
remarks: - If a mask has already been created, it is rebuilt with the new tolerance.
- A value out of range raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the tolerance in scientific notation, for example `4.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:MASK:Y 0.48    /*Sets the vertical tolerance to 0.48 div.*/
:MASK:Y?    /*The query returns 4.800000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Creates the mask from the source channel of the displayed record, using the current X and Y tolerances.
remarks: - If the source has no waveform, `-230,"Data corrupt or stale" source has no waveform` is raised.

commands.desc: Resets the pass, fail and total counts of the mask test to zero.
Starts or stops the mask test (runs or stops the acquisition), or queries its state.
remarks: - The mask test must be enabled (:MASK:ENABle ON); otherwise `-224,"Illegal parameter value" mask is off` is raised.
- `RUN` starts the acquisition; if the trigger sweep is Single it is changed to Auto. `STOP` stops the acquisition.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `RUN` when the mask test is enabled and the acquisition is running, otherwise `STOP`.
commands.example:
:MASK:OPER RUN    /*Starts the mask test.*/
:MASK:OPER?    /*The query returns RUN.*/

commands.desc: Queries the number of failed waveforms of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `12`.

commands.desc: Queries the number of passed waveforms of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `4988`.

commands.desc: Queries the total number of tested waveforms (passed + failed) of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `5000`.

commands.desc: Creates the mask from a loaded reference, like Create from ref in the Mask menu.
remarks: - The reference also becomes the working reference slot.
- An empty slot generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" that reference is empty`; an argument that is not a reference generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.example: :MASK:CRE:REF R1    /*Builds the mask around reference R1.*/

commands.desc: Deletes the mask.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
