commands.desc: Turns modulation on or off, or queries its status. Turning it on keeps the current modulation type, or selects AM if none is set.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the modulation type. Selecting a type also turns modulation on.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns NONE, AM, FM or PM. NONE means that modulation is off.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:TYP FM    /*Selects frequency modulation.*/
:SOUR:MOD:TYP?    /*The query returns FM.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the AM depth in percent. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the depth in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the FM frequency deviation in Hz. Values below 0.01 Hz are raised to 0.01 Hz.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the deviation in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the PM phase deviation in degrees. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the deviation in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the frequency of the internal modulating waveform in Hz. One value is shared by AM, FM and PM, so <type> may be any of them. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FREQ 1000    /*Sets a 1 kHz modulating frequency.*/
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FREQ?    /*The query returns 1.000000E+03.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the shape of the internal modulating waveform. One shape is shared by AM, FM and PM.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns SIN, SQU, TRI, RAMP, NRAM or NOIS.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FUNC TRI    /*Modulates with a triangle.*/
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FUNC?    /*The query returns TRI.*/

commands.desc: Loads an arbitrary waveform from a file and selects the ARB shape.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - The file holds one sample per line, or CSV rows; the samples may have any scale.
- The path refers to the file system of the instrument running OOS; without a path `arb.csv` in the save folder is loaded.
- When the file holds no usable wave, the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" no wave in <path>`.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

subsystems.title: Calibration and Identification Commands
subsystems.intro: The :CALibrate commands run the self-calibration of the analog front end. The :IDENtify? query runs automatic signal identification on the current record. Neither is a passive read.

commands.desc: Starts self-calibration of the specified channel, or of all channels when <ch> is 0. The optional ZERO keyword selects the zero-offset calibration option; the optional ADC keyword also calibrates the ADC cores. Calibration runs in the background; poll :CALibrate:STATus?.
params: 0 to 4 (0 = all channels; larger values are treated as 4, non-numeric values as 0)
remarks: - Disconnect all signals from the inputs before starting. Calibration changes the stored calibration data and is not a passive diagnostic.
- Calibration requires the hardware acquisition source; with a file or simulated source, :CALibrate:STATus? reports that hardware is needed.
- The command does not report errors; check :CALibrate:STATus?.
- ZERO and ADC may be given in either order.
commands.example:
:CAL:STAR 0         /*Starts self-calibration of all channels.*/
:CAL:STAR 2,ZERO    /*Starts calibration of CH2 with the zero option.*/
:CAL:STAR 0,ADC     /*Calibrates all channels and the ADC cores.*/

commands.desc: Cancels a running self-calibration.
Queries the status of the self-calibration.
commands.returns: The query returns a free-text status line: `idle`, `starting ...`, `<percent> % <step>` while running, `done: <summary>` or `failed: <reason>` after a run, or `needs the hardware source` when calibration is not possible.

commands.desc: Runs signal identification on the current record of the channels that are on and returns the findings. The query also updates the identification shown in the UI.
remarks: - This query is not passive: it starts an analysis and may show a message on the screen.
commands.returns: The query returns the findings separated by `;`, each in the format `CH<a>[+CH<b>] <summary> (<confidence> %)`. It returns an empty line when nothing is found.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the analysis deskew of a channel or reference, in seconds: a time shift applied to that trace in the analysis.
remarks: - This is not the probe deskew of `:CHANnel<n>:TCALibrate`.
- An invalid source or a time outside the range generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the time in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-09`.
commands.example:
:CAL:DESK CHAN2,1e-9    /*Shifts CH2 by 1 ns in the analysis.*/
:CAL:DESK? CHAN2        /*The query returns 1.000000E-09.*/

commands.desc: Lines up the shown traces near the view by setting their analysis deskew, like Auto deskew.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Sets the analysis deskew of every trace back to 0.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

subsystems.title: :SYSTem Commands
subsystems.intro: The :SYSTem commands read the error queue, give direct access to every setting stored in a setup file, report diagnostic state and control the measurement logger.

commands.desc: Queries and removes the oldest entry of the error queue. Read repeatedly until `0,"No error"` is returned.
remarks: - The queue holds up to 20 entries of at most 256 bytes each; when it overflows, error -350 is queued.
- Typical codes: -113 undefined header, -221 settings conflict, -224 illegal parameter value, -230 data unavailable, -241 hardware missing, -256 file name not found.
commands.returns: The query returns `<code>,"<message>"`, optionally followed by a space and detail text, for example `-113,"Undefined header" :FOO`.

commands.desc: Reads the whole instrument setup as a block, or applies a setup sent as a block.
params: The text of a setup file
remarks: - Use the long form: the short form `:SYST:SET` is the single-setting command `:SYSTem:SET`.
- The block holds the same text as a saved setup file. Send it back unchanged to restore the setup; a semicolon or line feed inside a definite-length block does not end the command.
- The setting form also accepts the setup text without a block header.
- An argument that is not a setup generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by `setup block` or by the reason.
commands.returns: The query returns a definite-length block `#9<nine-digit length><setup text>`.
commands.example:
:SYSTem:SETup?                  /*The query returns #9000012345 followed by the setup text.*/
:SYSTem:SETup #9000012345...    /*Applies the setup read before.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current value of one setup-file setting.
remarks: - Keys that are only stored when they differ from their default (for example `ch1.label`) return an empty reply while at the default.
commands.returns: The query returns the value text exactly as it appears in a setup file; it returns an empty line for an unknown key.

commands.desc: Queries one line of diagnostic state: frame rate and counters, run state, trigger status and timing figures.
commands.returns: The query returns a single line in the format `fps <f> frames <n> records <n> run <Run|Stop> status <status> t <s> step <ms> ms (acq <ms> draw <ms>) render <ms> ms present <ms> ms edges <a> <b> <c> <d> off <x> <y> parts meas <ms> analyse <ms> pane <ms> max <ms> ms[ gpu layers ...][ gpu panel ...] graphics <gpu|cpu> hdmi <off|<w>x<h> <mode>>`. The `gpu` parts appear only while the GPU draws.
commands.example: :SYST:STAT?    /*The query returns one diagnostic line beginning with fps.*/

commands.desc: Starts or stops the measurement logger. When started, the current measurement readouts are written to a new CSV log file in the save directory of the instrument.
remarks: - The logger does not start when no measurement is active; a message is shown instead.
- The log file is written on the instrument running OOS, not on the remote client. The interval is set with `:SYSTem:LOG:INTerval`; `:SYSTem:LOG:FILE?` and `:SYSTem:LOG:INFO?` report the file.
- An invalid argument generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while the logger writes a file, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:SYST:LOG ON    /*Starts logging the measurements.*/
:SYST:LOG?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the interval of the measurement logger, in seconds.
remarks: - Any positive value is accepted and set to the nearest listed interval.
- 0, a negative value or a value that is not a number generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the interval in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+01`.

commands.desc: Queries the log file the measurement logger is writing.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the path of the file on the instrument running OOS; an empty line when the logger is off.
commands.example: :SYST:LOG:FILE?    /*The query returns an empty line while the logger is off.*/

commands.desc: Queries the state of the measurement logger.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `<file name>: <n> rows` while logging, otherwise `<n> measurements, off`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the system date of the instrument.
remarks: - The clock is set like the Set the clock keyboard of System > Date and time; the other part of the date and time is kept.
- Anything other than three integers, or a date or time that is not valid, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `YYYY,MM,DD` in local time, for example `2026,11,16`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the system time of the instrument.
remarks: - The clock is set like the Set the clock keyboard of System > Date and time; the other part of the date and time is kept.
- Anything other than three integers, or a date or time that is not valid, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `hh,mm,ss` in local time, for example `14,30,00`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the time zone of the instrument.
remarks: - The value is the one entered in the Time zone row of System > Date and time.
- A zone that is not accepted generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the zone, for example `UTC0`.

commands.desc: Turns time synchronisation over the network (NTP) on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the NTP server.
params: A host name or address, or DHCP
remarks: - DHCP uses the server announced by the network.
- A server that is not accepted generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the server, or `dhcp`.

commands.desc: Queries the state of the time synchronisation, as shown in System > Date and time.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns one line of text, for example `Off`.

commands.desc: Synchronises the clock with the NTP server now.
remarks: - This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the network name (host name) of the instrument.
remarks: - A name that is not a valid host name generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the name, for example `dho924s`.

commands.desc: Queries the IP address of the wired network interface.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the address, for example `192.168.1.20`.

commands.desc: Queries the MAC address of the wired network interface.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the address, or `-` when it is not known.

commands.desc: Queries the state of the wired network interface, as shown in System > Network.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns one line of text with the address and the link state.
commands.example: :SYST:COMM:LAN:STAT?    /*The query returns the address and the link state.*/

commands.desc: Turns the 10 Mbit/s retry of the wired network on or off, or queries its state: when the link does not come up, it is tried again at 10 Mbit/s.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Queries the state of the wireless network, as shown in System > Network.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns one line of text, for example `no stick` when no Wi-Fi stick is plugged in.

commands.desc: Scans for wireless networks.
remarks: - Read the result with `:SYSTem:WLAN:NETWorks?`.
- This command has no query form. Sending the query also performs the action and then generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Queries the wireless networks found by the last scan.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns one network per line; the last line is `Other network ...`.

commands.desc: Queries the saved wireless networks.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns one network name per line; an empty line when none is saved.

commands.desc: Deletes a saved wireless network.
params: 1 to the number of saved networks
remarks: - `<n>` counts the lines of `:SYSTem:WLAN:SAVed?` from 1.
- A number outside the range generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
- While the wireless network is busy, the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"` followed by the reason.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Turns the SCPI socket service on or off, or queries its state.
params: Keyword, needed to switch the service off
remarks: - Switching the service off ends the SCPI session that sends the command; it needs the argument CONFIRM. Without it the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Switching SCPI off needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:SYST:REM:SERV:SCPI?               /*The query returns 1.*/
:SYST:REM:SERV:SCPI OFF,CONFIRM    /*Switches the SCPI service off.*/

commands.desc: Turns the VXI-11 service on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Turns the Telnet service on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Turns the web page on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Turns the mDNS announcement on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Locks or unlocks the touch screen, or queries whether it is locked.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.

commands.desc: Queries the system information page: unit, software, temperatures, limits, load and the acquisition now.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns several lines: a `# <section>` line before each section, then `<name>,<value>` lines.

commands.desc: Sets or queries whether the screen is drawn by the GPU or by the CPU.
remarks: - Whether the GPU really draws is shown by the `gpu` part of `:SYSTem:STATe?`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `GPU` or `CPU`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the action of the Quick key.
remarks: - The value is the option text of the menu row; case, spaces and punctuation are ignored, so `Save setup` and `"Save setup"` select the same option.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the option text in capitals with spaces written as `_`, for example `SAVE_SETUP`.

commands.desc: Switches the instrument off.
remarks: - Without the argument CONFIRM the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Power off needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- While an update job is running, the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" an update job is running`.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Restarts the instrument.
remarks: - Without the argument CONFIRM the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Restart needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- While an update job is running, the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" an update job is running`.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Queries the state of the software update, as shown in System > Update.
remarks: - This command is query-only; the command form generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns several lines of text.

commands.desc: Goes back to the software version installed before the last update.
remarks: - Without the argument CONFIRM the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Roll back needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- When there is nothing to roll back to, a message is shown.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Installs a software update from a file.
params: Path of the update file on the instrument, in quotes
remarks: - Without the argument CONFIRM the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Update needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- A file that cannot be read generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value" <path>: <reason>`; an update that is refused generates error `-221,"Settings conflict"` followed by the reason.
- Follow the progress with `:SYSTem:UPDate:STATus?`.
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the boot mode: Persist keeps OOS as the system, One-shot makes the next power-on start the stock firmware.
params: Keyword, needed to change the mode
remarks: - Changing the mode needs the argument CONFIRM; without it the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Changing the boot mode needs the argument CONFIRM`. Setting the mode that is already set needs no CONFIRM.
- The long or the short form of the keyword is accepted.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `PERS` or `ONES`.
commands.example:
:SYST:BOOT?                /*The query returns ONES.*/
:SYST:BOOT PERS,CONFIRM    /*Keeps OOS as the system.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the ADC clock that applies from the next start of the acquisition, in hertz.
params: Keyword, needed to change the clock
remarks: - The value must be one of the listed clocks (within 0.1 %); other values generate error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.

- Changing the clock needs the argument CONFIRM; without it the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Overclock needs the argument CONFIRM`. Setting the clock that is already set needs no CONFIRM.
commands.returns: The query returns the clock in scientific notation, for example `1.250000E+09`.

commands.desc: Prepares the return to the stock firmware, like Back to stock in the System menu: a message says what the next power-on does.
remarks: - Without the argument CONFIRM the command generates error `-221,"Settings conflict" Back to stock needs the argument CONFIRM`.
- With boot mode One-shot the stock firmware starts at the next power-cycle; with Persist, set the boot mode to One-shot first (`:SYSTem:BOOT ONEShot,CONFIRM`).
- This command has no query form; the query generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
